'''Jerzy Lewandowski''' ({{IPA|pol|lɛvanˈdɔfskʲi|lang}}; 15 September 1959 – 8 October 2024) was a Polish theoretical physicist best known for his extensive research into [[general relativity]] and [[quantum gravity]].

==Biography==
Lewandowski was professor of physics at the [[University of Warsaw]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerzy Lewandowski|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=yRtnPg8AAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=5 March 2021|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> He received his doctorate in [[Warsaw]] under [[Andrzej Trautman]].<ref name="fuw">{{Cite web |date=2024-10-16 |title=Remembrance of Professor Jerzy Lewandowski – Edward Malec – Polish Society on Relativity |url=https://potor.fuw.edu.pl/en/2024/10/16/remembrance-of-professor-jerzy-lewandowski-edward-malec/ |access-date=2026-06-21 |language=en-US}}</ref> He worked closely with [[Abhay Ashtekar]] at [[Pennsylvania State University]] in the 1990s on the mathematical justification of [[Loop quantum gravity|Loop Quantum Gravity]] (LQG).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ashtekar |first=Abhay |last2=Lewandowski |first2=Jerzy |date=2004-08-07 |title=Background independent quantum gravity: a status report |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/21/15/R01 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |volume=21 |issue=15 |pages=R53–R152 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/21/15/R01 |issn=0264-9381|arxiv=gr-qc/0404018 }}</ref> Among other things, he was at the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics|Erwin Schrödinger Institute]] in [[Vienna]] and at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] in Golm near [[Potsdam]].<ref>https://www.fuw.edu.pl/tl_files/aktualnosci/nekrologi/Jerzy_Lewandowski_kondolencje.pdf

</ref><ref name="fuw" />

He dealt with [[Physical cosmology|cosmological models]] and the [[Black hole thermodynamics|entropy of black holes]] in the LQG. In 2010 he and his colleagues investigated a scalar field together with the [[gravitational field]] as part of LQG and were able to show the origin of a time as the ratio of the scalar to the gravitational field, and the [[Quantization (physics)|quantization]] of the gravitational field.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Domagała|first=Marcin|last2=Giesel|first2=Kristina|last3=Kamiński|first3=Wojciech|last4=Lewandowski|first4=Jerzy|date=18 November 2010|title=Gravity quantized: Loop quantum gravity with a scalar field|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.82.104038|journal=Physical Review D|volume=82|issue=10|doi=10.1103/physrevd.82.104038|issn=1550-7998|arxiv=1009.2445}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The birth of time: Quantum loops describe the evolution of the Universe|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2010/12/101216095014.htm|access-date=5 March 2021|website=ScienceDaily|language=en}}</ref>

Lewandowski died on 8 October 2024, at the age of 65.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. dr hab. Jerzy Lewandowski |url=https://www.fuw.edu.pl/home.html |website=fuw.edu.pl |access-date=10 October 2024}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* With Ashtekar ''Background independent quantum gravity: a status report'', Classical and Quantum Gravity, Band 21, 2004, R 53 [http://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0404018 Arxiv]
* Abhay Ashtekar, Jerzy Lewandowski, [[Donald Marolf]], Jose Mourao, Thomas Thiemann ''Quantization of diffeomorphism invariant theories of connections with local degrees of freedom'', J. Mathematical Physics, Band 36, 1995, S. 6456–6493, [http://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9504018 Arxiv]
* With Ashtekar ''Quantum theory of Gravity I. Area Operators'', Classical and Quantum Gravity, Band 14, 1997, A 55–82,  [http://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9602046 Arxiv], Volume II: ''Volume Operators'', [http://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9711031 Arxiv]
* With [[Martin Bojowald]], Ashtekar ''Mathematical structure of loop quantum cosmology'', Adv.Theor.Math.Phys., Band 7, 2003, S. 233–268, [http://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0304074 Arxiv]
